subject: Sandbox provisioning + routing smoke test — POC kickoff
messages:
From: Rachel Park <rachel@sparkbridge.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC kickoff — hands-on session + env prep

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. SparkBridge is ready to kick off the two-week POC and we'd like to schedule a hands-on working session where your team can help us:

- Provision a sandbox API key and a short-lived staging account for our devs
- Confirm VPC allowlist / IP ranges and any peering details required for our private subnets
- Walk through routing configuration (prompt routing, model variant fallbacks) and run the routing "smoke" tests
- Run a quick load test of a few representative prompts (token sizes + parallel sessions) to validate latency targets

Proposed windows next week (all PT): Tue 11/9 10:00–11:30, Wed 11/10 09:00–10:30, Thu 11/11 13:00–14:30. We prefer Tue morning if available.

Also: can you confirm what staging endpoint hostname we should point to, and whether we need to provide subnet/CIDR info for allowlisting? I'll loop in our infra lead if you need anything from our side.

Attaching a short internal agenda.

Thanks,
Rachel Park
Chief Data Officer | SparkBridge AI
rachel@sparkbridge.ai

Attachment: sparkbridge-poc-agenda.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Park <rachel@sparkbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: POC kickoff — hands-on session + env prep

Rachel — thanks, that works. Diego/Ava this is the SparkBridge POC (deal SB-2026-0473). Can you help with the infra prep and running the smoke/load tests? Quick asks: 

- Diego: can you provide the staging endpoint hostname and the IP ranges we should ask SparkBridge to allowlist? Also assemble a short routing smoke-test checklist we can run during the session.
- Ava: can you lead the prompt review and prepare 6–8 representative prompts (short/med/long) so we can exercise KV cache and token limits?
- Marissa: I'll need you on the call for environment walkthrough and to run the load harness.

I suggest we target Tue 2026-11-09 10:00 PT (Rachel preference). If Diego/Ava need a different slot, call it out. I'll send a calendar invite after we confirm.

Proposed agenda (30–90 mins depending on depth):
1) Quick introductions + goals (5–10m)
2) Sandbox provisioning & keys (10m)
3) VPC/allowlist & staging endpoint confirmation (10m)
4) Prompt review (15–20m)
5) Routing smoke test (15m)
6) Short load run + metrics review (15–30m)
7) Next steps / rollout plan

Attaching SparkBridge's agenda from Rachel for context.

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
log an_wright@redwood.ai

Attachment: sparkbridge-poc-agenda.pdf (forwarded)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: POC kickoff — hands-on session + env prep

Logan — happy to own infra/run tests. Quick answers and what I need from SparkBridge: 

1) Staging endpoint (recommended): stg-us-west.redwood.ai:443 (TLS). Use this for API host, path /v1/generate or our SDK config; we'll ensure it routes to the POC tenant.

2) Allowlist: the POC can be run either with IP allowlist or optional VPC peering. For IP allowlist we need the customer egress ranges; our minimal set for the session is: 34.216.0.0/16, 54.185.0.0/16, 3.234.0.0/16 (these are our outbound NAT pools in us-west). If they prefer VPC peering we need their VPC CIDRs and a proposed subnet for the peering tunnel.

3) Sandbox keys: I can generate a short-lived API key with the following limits: 200k tokens total, rate limit 30 rps, token cap 4096 per request. If that looks good I'll provision and drop a stub credentials file in the thread (sandbox-credentials-stub.txt).

4) Routing smoke test checklist: I'll run these steps during the call —
   - Verify model selection via X-model header (gpt-open/rdw-2b)
   - Exercise fallback: primary model OOM -> automatic fallback to quantized variant
   - Validate prefix caching: identical prompt repeated 3x -> ensure second/third calls return <50% token compute cost
   - Measure p95 latency on 3 prompt sizes (64, 512, 2048 tokens)

I'll attach the checklist and can demo the load harness. If the customer wants a deeper load run we'll schedule a separate window.

Attachment: routing-smoke-test-checklist.md

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai

From: Rachel Park <rachel@sparkbridge.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Agenda look good. For the load test, let's keep the first run light (10 concurrent sessions across 3 prompt sizes) — we can schedule a heavier run if we need later. We'll also bring our privacy/security lead to verify that the sandbox keys will be scoped appropriately.

Thanks — looking forward,
Rachel
